section_summary: This section documents Japanese budgets, war spending, bond issues, taxation, savings and currency circulation from 1941 through the 1944–45 fiscal year. It includes embassy reports, press translations, State Department analyses and cross-reference notes. A separate group of letters records American holders’ inquiries about Japanese government, Yokohama and Tokyo Electric Light bonds.

subfiles.title: Closing page of Japanese government budget statement
subfiles.about: The speaker urges patriotic saving and approval of government bills.
subfiles.summary: Concludes by urging patriotic saving, national unity and prompt approval of government bills.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs note on Tokyo despatch No. 6014
subfiles.about: Summarizes the Japanese 1942–43 budget report.
subfiles.summary: Highlights increased military spending, reliance on bonds, stronger bond absorption, projected national income and the absence of foreign borrowing.

subfiles.title: National Budget for Japan—1942–43 Fiscal Year
subfiles.about: Transmits the Commercial Attaché’s report on Japan’s 1942–43 national budget.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch forwarding the report and suggesting distribution to the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce.

subfiles.title: National Budget for Japan—1942–43 Fiscal Year
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japan’s 1942–43 general, military and colonial budgets.
subfiles.summary: Williams compares the 1942–43 budget with the preceding year and details ministry allocations, war appropriations, bond financing, taxation and national savings. He estimates military appropriations since July 1937 at about ¥47.1 billion and discusses the ability to finance them domestically. The report also covers income estimates and colonial agricultural and infrastructure spending.

subfiles.title: Economic and financial developments in Japan, December 1941–June 1942
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch reporting Japanese economic and financial developments.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Grew’s June 3, 1942 despatch filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Commercial Attaché’s financial and economic report material
subfiles.about: Points to material prepared before December 8, 1941 for regular reports.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Grew despatch filed under 894.50/163.

subfiles.title: Supplementary Budget, 1941–42 Fiscal Year
subfiles.from: Frank S. Williams, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports supplementary Japanese Diet appropriations for 1941–42.
subfiles.summary: Details additional general, war and special-account appropriations approved by an extraordinary Diet session, with tables for bond issues, ministry spending and colonial accounts.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about frozen Yokohama Specie Bank assets
subfiles.about: Asks about assets frozen at the Yokohama Specie Bank in New York.
subfiles.summary: Congressional inquiry concerning frozen Japanese bank assets and claims.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Crawford inquiry to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards Crawford’s inquiry to Foreign Funds Control.
subfiles.summary: Sends Crawford’s letter to the Treasury office with jurisdiction over frozen assets.

subfiles.title: Reply to Fred L. Crawford
subfiles.about: Explains referral of his frozen-assets inquiry to Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Crawford’s letter and directs him to Treasury’s Foreign Funds Control Division.

subfiles.title: Japan’s General Accounts Budget for 1943 Fiscal Year
subfiles.about: Transmits translated Japanese press reports on the 1943–44 general budget.
subfiles.summary: Notes a nearly ¥10 billion general budget and undisclosed military expenditures.

subfiles.title: Japan’s General Accounts Budget for 1943 Fiscal Year
subfiles.about: Gives the proposed 1943–44 general accounts budget and ministry allocations.
subfiles.summary: Lists estimated receipts, expenditures and ministry allotments totaling roughly ¥10 billion, followed by a speech about reducing ministry requests.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Buenos Aires budget despatch to Chungking
subfiles.about: Sends the Buenos Aires despatch on Japan’s 1943–44 budget.
subfiles.summary: Forwards despatch No. 7847 and its enclosure for confidential information.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum for Japanese 1943–44 budget analysis
subfiles.about: Introduces an analysis based on monitored Japanese broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the attached report’s view that bond absorption and production supported Japan’s rising war budget.

subfiles.title: Japan’s National Budget for the Fiscal Year 1943–44
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japan’s 1943–44 budget using monitored broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Williams compares general and military budgets, estimating total appropriations at ¥39.34 billion, including ¥27 billion for extraordinary military spending. He examines revenue, bond absorption, subsidies, savings and income. He concludes that Japan appeared able to sustain the higher budget through bonds, taxes and industrial production.

subfiles.title: Japan’s National Budget for the Fiscal Year 1943–44, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: Repeats Williams’s analysis of Japan’s 1943–44 budget.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the report on general and military appropriations, revenue, bonds, subsidies, national income and savings.

subfiles.title: Reconvening of the Japanese eighty-first Diet
subfiles.about: Points to a letter on the Diet session and budget measures.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Ford’s February 5 letter filed under 894.032/219.

subfiles.title: Note on Chinese editorial about Japanese war finance
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Ta Kung Pao editorial predicting Japanese financial collapse.
subfiles.summary: Notes the editorial’s figures and argument that debt, inflation and Allied attacks threatened Japan’s finances.

subfiles.title: Chinese Editorial Comment on Japanese Financial Situation
subfiles.about: Transmits a translation of a Chinese editorial on Japan’s war finances.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the editorial’s claims about Japan’s 1943 budget, indebtedness, taxation, currency circulation and investments in Manchuria and China.

subfiles.title: Japan’s War Finance on Brink of Collapse
subfiles.about: Argues that wartime borrowing and inflation make Japanese finances vulnerable.
subfiles.summary: The editorial compares Japanese budgets with earlier years and Allied spending, discusses debt, taxation and currency issuance, and calls for attacks on multiple fronts. It links Japanese investment in Manchuria and North China to resource extraction.

subfiles.title: Japanese National Income Estimated at US$11 Billion for 1943
subfiles.doc_type: embassy despatch with translated press item
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese estimates of 1942 and 1943 national income and wartime claims on it.
subfiles.summary: Cites Finance Minister Kaya’s reported estimates of ¥45 billion in 1942 and ¥50 billion in 1943, with more than two-thirds directed to state needs.

subfiles.title: Mary Powell Purdy’s Japanese bond registration request
subfiles.about: Asks the Department to record her Japanese government bond.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a $1,000 Japanese government bond and requests that her interest be recorded.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mary Powell Purdy
subfiles.about: Acknowledges her bond information and requests citizenship details.
subfiles.summary: Says the information will be filed and asks when and how she became an American citizen.

subfiles.title: J. P. Christensen’s inquiry about Japanese and Yokohama bonds
subfiles.about: Seeks advice after a New York banking official rejected his bond claim.
subfiles.summary: Asks about recovery prospects for Japanese government and City of Yokohama bonds.

subfiles.title: Reply to J. P. Christensen
subfiles.about: Responds to his rejected bond claim.
subfiles.summary: Explains the Department’s usual practice and invites details of the bonds and Christensen’s U.S. citizenship.

subfiles.title: Mary Powell Purdy’s bond and citizenship details
subfiles.about: Supplies purchase and citizenship information requested by the Department.
subfiles.summary: Says she bought the bond in 1930 and was born in Amityville, New York.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Mary Powell Purdy
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of her further bond information.
subfiles.summary: States that her letter has been received and filed.

subfiles.title: Statement regarding Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Records Christensen’s bond purchases, custody, rejected claim and citizenship.
subfiles.summary: Identifies two bonds, their purchase prices, New York custody and Christensen’s naturalization.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to J. P. Christensen
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Christensen’s sworn bond statement.
subfiles.summary: States that his statement has been received and filed.

subfiles.title: War expenditures of Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a confidential telegram containing Japanese war-expenditure data.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram No. 3205, filed under 862.51/5075.

subfiles.title: Second Supplementary Budget 1943–1944 Adopted by the 82nd Session of the Japanese Diet
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japan’s June 1943 supplementary budget.
subfiles.summary: Reports a roughly ¥620 million supplementary appropriation, raising total 1943–44 budget authority to nearly ¥40 billion. Notes rice subsidies, colonial food-control accounts and possible funding for tighter industrial controls.

subfiles.title: Japanese national income, expenditure and savings estimates
subfiles.about: Relays published estimates for Japanese income, consumption, loans and savings.
subfiles.summary: Compares 1941–43 figures and reports projected 1943 savings of ¥27 billion.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese bond claim forms
subfiles.about: Asks how a client may file a claim on Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Requests forms for an unnamed client who owns Japanese government bonds.

subfiles.title: Reply to Max Michael on bond claims
subfiles.about: Explains how to submit bond information without a special form.
subfiles.summary: Lists the details needed for a bondholder statement and explains that no special claim form is required. Page 228 is another copy of the reply.

subfiles.title: Max Michael’s statement of clients’ Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Identifies Japanese government and Tokyo Electric Light bonds held by four clients.
subfiles.summary: Lists bonds, face values, numbers, purchase prices, maturity dates and overdue coupons for Aurie Baynes Arnold, Eugenia Arnold Blount, Jennie Arnold Dorsey and O. H. Arnold Jr.

subfiles.title: Request for Michael clients’ citizenship and price details
subfiles.about: Requests addresses, citizenship details and clarification of a bond purchase price.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Michael’s filing and asks for further client and price information.

subfiles.title: Max Michael’s supplemental client information
subfiles.about: Provides clients’ birthplace, address and corrected bond prices.
subfiles.summary: Reports that all four clients were born in Georgia and corrects the two-bond price to $940 each.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Max Michael
subfiles.about: Acknowledges supplemental information on his clients’ Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: States that Michael’s further letter has been received and filed.

subfiles.title: Japanese budget for 1944–45 and circulation of paper currency
subfiles.about: Transmits German press translations on Japan’s budget, currency and savings.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for three translated German press items.

subfiles.title: Japanese Special Budget Estimates for the Conduct of the War
subfiles.about: Reports proposed 1944–45 Japanese war-budget financing.
subfiles.summary: Gives a ¥38 billion war budget and compares expected loan requirements with the preceding year.

subfiles.title: Japanese Circulation of Paper Currency
subfiles.about: Reports rising banknote circulation in Japan, Korea and Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Provides 1942–43 currency figures and the finance minister’s explanation of rising cash needs.

subfiles.title: Japanese Savings
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese official savings and income targets for 1944–45.
subfiles.summary: Projects ¥60 billion national income and ¥36 billion savings, alongside taxes and government requirements.

subfiles.title: Japanese budget for 1944–45 and circulation of paper currency, duplicate despatch
subfiles.about: Repeats the Bern despatch transmitting three German press translations.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the cover despatch on budget, currency and savings.

subfiles.title: Japanese Special Budget Estimates for the Conduct of the War, duplicate enclosure
subfiles.about: Repeats the translated item on 1944–45 Japanese war-budget estimates.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the report on the ¥38 billion war budget and loan requirements.
